name: Fieldquote
headline:
Turn field findings
into repair work.
sub: Your technician finds a fault. Your office gets a checked repair quote to approve—without rebuilding the visit from scattered notes.
buyer: Commercial HVAC service companies with a busy maintenance book and an office team preparing repair quotes.
problem: The visit is finished. The repair quote is not.
pains: Technicians describe the fault in notes, photos and calls. The office has to piece it together.
Missing model numbers and uncertain parts send the quote back to the technician.
Repair opportunities wait while customers still need a clear price and a next step.
offer: We turn your technicians’ completed findings into clear, approval-ready repair quotes inside your existing workflow, so useful repair opportunities reach the customer sooner.
system: An intake and quote-preparation workflow: read the visit, match approved equipment and price-book records, flag gaps, prepare the quote, then hand it to your estimator.
scope: One service team and one repair category
Visit-note intake and equipment matching
Approved price-book lookup and quote draft
Estimator review, handoff and status tracking
exclude: No AI diagnosis, guessed parts, autonomous pricing or replacement of your field-service platform.
dependency: Sample visits, a current price book, equipment records, permission to connect the existing software, and an estimator who owns approvals.
accept: On an agreed test set, each complete visit creates a traceable draft; unknown parts block the quote; nothing sends without estimator approval.
fit: Start with a team producing enough repair quotes to have a measurable queue. Reject the custom build if its field-service platform already covers the process well.
alternative: BuildOps already combines service, quoting and CRM. Start by checking the customer’s native setup; our possible opening is disconnected intake or a specific integration gap, not rebuilding BuildOps.
evidence: A named commercial HVAC customer describes same-day quoting and connected service operations. This supports the workflow’s relevance; it does not establish demand for our custom service.
strength: Named vendor case; custom-service demand untested
acquire: Call service managers at regional commercial HVAC firms. Offer to trace three recent maintenance visits through to the quote. Use a short screen demo in a personal follow-up email; broad ads come after a repeated pain is confirmed.
question: Show us the last repair quote that took too long. What was missing, who touched it, and when did the customer receive it?
extra: Additional repair wins could matter more than time saved, but we have not assumed any increase in sales.
complexity: Moderate · field-service integration and price-book quality
input_text: “RTU-04 has a worn belt. Photo attached. Recommend replacement. Need the exact belt size checked.”
steps: The visit note and equipment photo arrive together.
The workflow links the asset and prepares the repair description.
The belt size is uncertain. Pricing stays blocked until the estimator checks it.
Simulated estimator action: confirms the approved part and checks the price.
The approved quote is ready for the normal send process. It is not a sold job yet.
exception: Asset not found. Route to the estimator; do not invent equipment or a price.
deal: Optional outcome target: reduce visit-to-approved-quote time. Set the target only after measuring a sample; do not guarantee extra sales.
route: Implementation/configuration first; custom intake only if the gap survives the native-software check.

name: Changeproof
headline:
You did the extra work.
Make it billable.
sub: Turn field notes, labour and photos into a complete change-order request—before the evidence disappears into someone’s phone.
buyer: Electrical, mechanical and drywall subcontractors handling recurring extra work on commercial projects.
owner: Owner, commercial manager or project director
problem: Extra work happens on site. The paperwork falls behind.
pains: The crew completes extra work, but the instruction, hours and photos live in different places.
Project managers chase missing detail days later, when memories are already fading.
Requests arrive late or incomplete and become harder to substantiate.
offer: We connect your field records to your change-order process, so extra work becomes a complete, priced request your project manager can review and submit.
system: An evidence-to-request workflow: capture the instruction, link labour and materials, check required evidence, apply approved rates, and assemble the request for a project manager.
scope: One project and one extra-work workflow
Mobile note/photo intake linked to the job
Evidence checklist and approved rate lookup
Draft request, review queue and submission log
exclude: No automatic entitlement decisions, contract interpretation, fabricated signatures or promise that the main contractor will pay.
dependency: Project rules, approved rates, real sample extra-work records, a field champion and the project manager responsible for submission.
accept: Every pilot request links to its source records; missing authorisation blocks submission; the project manager can revise, approve and trace the final packet.
fit: Suitable when extra-work records genuinely get lost between field and office. If a configured Clearstory workflow fixes it, implement that instead of selling redundant custom software.
alternative: Clearstory already supplies digital extra-work tags, pricing, requests and integrations. A custom layer needs a specific existing-system or capture gap.
evidence: PCI describes lost or incomplete field tags and a rollout of Clearstory. This is a named example of the problem and an established alternative, not evidence of an untouched market.
strength: Named vendor case and existing paid platform
acquire: Target project directors at regional subcontractors through association directories and LinkedIn. Call about the last disputed or late extra-work request; send a walkthrough using a redacted example they provide.
question: Which extra-work request was last delayed or rejected because the supporting records were missing?
extra: Recovering previously unbilled work is a separate upside. Only count it after entitlement, approval and collection are established; it is not included here.
complexity: Moderate · project rules and rate control
input_text: Level 3 · reroute cable tray around revised ductwork. Two electricians × 4 hours. Photos and site instruction attached.
steps: A foreman records the work while the details are still fresh.
Hours, photos and the site instruction are linked to the same job.
The instruction is present, but its approval status needs the project manager.
Simulated PM action: confirms the instruction and checks the approved rates.
The request is ready for submission with a traceable evidence pack. Payment is still the customer’s decision.
exception: Missing site instruction. Hold the request and assign the PM to obtain evidence; do not manufacture approval.
deal: Potential outcome target: complete eligible requests ready for review within an agreed interval. Do not promise payment of disputed work.
route: Configure the specialist platform first; integrate field capture if a genuine gap remains.

name: Loadclear
headline:
The load is delivered.
Get the invoice moving.
sub: Collect delivery documents, match them to the load and prepare the billing packet—without the office chasing every driver.
buyer: Regional trucking companies whose delivery documents delay invoicing across drivers or depots.
problem: The truck is back on the road. The invoice is still waiting.
pains: Delivery receipts arrive as photos, scans and attachments with missing load numbers.
Billing staff chase signatures and extra-charge receipts before an invoice can go out.
Completed loads sit unbilled while the team sorts the documents.
offer: We connect driver paperwork to your billing workflow, so complete deliveries become invoice-ready packets and missing documents get a clear owner.
system: A delivery-to-billing workflow: read uploaded documents, match the load, check customer-required paperwork, chase missing items internally, and prepare the packet for billing approval.
scope: One depot and one customer billing pattern
Document intake and load matching
Missing-document queue and internal reminders
Invoice packet preparation and billing handoff
exclude: No invented signatures, automatic accessorial approval, collection guarantee or unapproved invoice sending.
dependency: TMS access, customer billing requirements, sample delivery documents, duplicate rules and a billing approver.
accept: A complete sample packet matches the right load once; a missing signature or mismatch blocks billing; the billing team can inspect and approve the packet.
fit: Start where the office can show delivered loads waiting for paperwork. If its TMS or Vector deployment already does this, improve that configuration rather than duplicate it.
alternative: Vector already offers mobile capture and rendition billing. The agency opportunity is a scoped integration or rollout for a specific disconnected process, not a generic PDF-reading bot.
evidence: Tiger Lines describes manual document handling and connecting capture to billing. The case reports shorter delivery-to-invoice time; it is a vendor account, not proof of our proposed performance.
strength: Named vendor implementation; exact agency offer untested
acquire: Build a focused list of regional carriers, then call billing managers. Ask for their delivered-but-not-invoiced report. A personalised email with a mock packet supports the call; mass SMS is not the starting route.
question: How many delivered loads are waiting to be invoiced today, and which documents are holding them up?
extra: Earlier invoicing may release working capital. That is not new revenue, and payment timing still depends on customers.
complexity: Moderate · TMS access and document matching
input_text: Proof of delivery · Load 8421. Delivered to West Depot. Three pallets. Receiver signature is hard to read.
steps: The receipt arrives against the delivery record.
Load number and destination are checked against the transport system.
The receiver signature cannot be verified from this scan. Billing stays on hold.
Simulated staff action: a clearer receipt is supplied and reviewed.
The packet joins the billing queue with its supporting records. No invoice has been sent in this demo.
exception: Load number does not match the delivery destination. Quarantine the document; never attach it to a guessed load.
deal: Potential outcome target: reduce delivery-to-invoice-ready time for complete records. It is not a promise of collection or new revenue.
route: Existing document/billing product plus bounded TMS integration; verify access before quoting.

name: Exchangeflow
headline:
An exchange should not
be an office project.
sub: Connect the customer request, warehouse receipt and replacement order—so your team can resolve exchanges without chasing three systems.
buyer: Shopify retailers also using NetSuite, with enough exchanges to need a dedicated operations process.
owner: Head of ecommerce, operations director or customer-experience lead
problem: The customer wants another size. Your systems disagree.
pains: Support sees the request, the warehouse sees the parcel, and finance sees a different status.
Replacements wait on manual checks—or get released before the returned item is received.
Customers ask for updates while the team switches between tools to reconstruct what happened.
offer: We connect one clearly defined exchange flow across your store and back office, with a visible hold until the warehouse confirms the return and staff approve any exception.
system: A same-price exchange workflow: identify the order, draft the support response, check policy and stock, create a held request, then release it after the required warehouse event.
scope: One store and same-price size exchanges
Order, policy and stock lookups
Warehouse-receipt hold and release logic
Exception queue, status sync and audit trail
exclude: No full ERP migration, autonomous refunds, price-difference accounting or tax changes. AI drafts language; deterministic rules control financial and stock actions.
dependency: Shopify/NetSuite sandbox access, return policy, a warehouse event owner, integration licence review and finance approval of the test cases.
accept: A duplicate event cannot create a second exchange; no replacement releases before verified receipt; unavailable stock and policy exceptions stay in a staff queue.
fit: This is the advanced option. Skip small stores whose normal returns app already covers the whole process; target a demonstrable store-to-ERP gap.
alternative: Loop/Gorgias already share returns data. ZangaBee describes a Shopify–NetSuite workflow that became a Celigo template. Test that template before proposing custom code.
evidence: A provider describes a customer’s conditional exchange implementation, including waiting for a warehouse receipt. The client and sale value are not disclosed. This is an example of implementation work, not proof of our pricing.
acquire: Find ecommerce operations leads whose companies publicly use Shopify and NetSuite. Confirm the stack and exchange volume on a discovery call; demonstrate the hold-and-release workflow to operations and finance together.
question: Walk through the last exchange that needed support, warehouse and finance to intervene. Where did the status stop updating?
extra: Retained sales and repeat purchases are not included. This model values handling capacity only.
input_text: “My jacket arrived but medium is too small. Can I exchange it for a large?”
steps: The message is linked to the order and a response is drafted from the store policy.
The workflow checks the approved return window and available size.
The replacement stays on hold until the returned item is physically confirmed.
Simulated warehouse action: staff receive and inspect the returned item.
The approved replacement moves to fulfilment and the customer update is prepared.
exception: Large is out of stock. Keep the replacement on hold and ask support to offer approved options; never promise unavailable stock.
deal: Commit to the tested hold, duplicate protection and exception routing—not a guaranteed increase in retained revenue.
route: Template-led integration with an experienced ERP specialist. Not a first unsupported beginner build.

name: Shortlist
headline:
Great candidates.
Ready to present.
sub: Turn the CV and your interview notes into a clear, source-linked candidate brief—then give the recruiter the final say.
buyer: Specialist recruitment agencies preparing frequent bespoke candidate submissions for hiring managers.
owner: Agency founder or recruitment operations manager
problem: The candidate is ready. The submission is still being rewritten.
pains: Recruiters copy the same experience, salary and availability into another client template.
Interview notes and CV details conflict, so someone has to check the story before sending.
Hiring-manager feedback disappears across forwarded emails.
offer: We connect candidate records, interview notes and your client template to prepare accurate submission packs, with recruiter approval and a clear feedback handoff.
system: A submission-preparation workflow: extract supported facts, map them to the role brief, flag contradictions, format the profile, and prepare a client share for recruiter approval.
scope: One recruiting team and submission format
CV and approved interview-note intake
Fact-linked brief and contradiction checks
Recruiter approval and client feedback record
exclude: No automated candidate rejection or ranking, invented achievements, reference verification or sending personal data without authorised review.
dependency: Approved candidate data, the role brief, ATS access, retention/access rules and a recruiter who checks facts and permission to share.
accept: Each material claim traces to a source; conflicting salary or availability stays flagged; sharing requires recruiter approval; access can be revoked.
fit: A simple tool may be enough. Only sell implementation where bespoke templates, permissions or disconnected intake create a real recurring gap.
alternative: Candidately already provides Bullhorn-linked presentations and a client portal. Use or configure it where it fits; do not charge a custom-build fee to recreate the same feature.
evidence: A named boutique recruiter describes adopting connected candidate presentations and improving feedback flow. It supports the problem, but the existing product is a serious alternative to a custom build.
strength: Named vendor case; weakest custom-build differentiation
acquire: Approach specialist agency founders via LinkedIn and phone with a sample submission in their format. Ask to time the preparation of one real pack before proposing any integration.
question: What does your team still rewrite by hand after the CV and interview are complete, and why does your current ATS not handle it?
extra: Placement fees are not included. Faster presentation does not by itself establish extra placements.
complexity: Moderate · ATS access, privacy and source accuracy
input_text: Alex Morgan · Operations lead. CV: warehouse team leadership. Interview: available in four weeks. ATS record: two weeks.
steps: The CV, interview notes and job brief form the starting record.
The assistant drafts only claims supported by those records.
Two sources give different start dates. The draft stays unshared.
Simulated recruiter action: confirms four weeks and approves the brief for the named client.
The pack is ready to share, with feedback assigned back to the recruiter.
exception: A claimed certification has no supporting source. Remove the claim and ask the recruiter; do not infer it from the job title.
deal: Potential outcome target: reduce preparation time while passing an agreed factual-review checklist. Never guarantee placements.
route: Configure existing presentation software first. Custom work only for a verified gap.
